values.note: 36 drive-in sites plus two accessible sites (numbered 1-38 on the DNR map), and a group camp for up to 50.

sites.source: MN DNR record sft00020, facility cmp00018 (camping: drive_in_campsites 36, campsites 2, accessible_campsites 2, group_campsites 1; 'A group camp is available for up to 50 people') + DNR facility map cmp00018.pdf (sites 1-38), read 2026-11-11

hookups.source: MN DNR record sft00020, facility cmp00018 ('The campground is considered "primitive," designed to furnish only the camper's basic needs. Campsites have a cleared area, a fire ring, and a picnic table.'), read 2026-11-11

values.note: Individual sites are first come; the fee is paid online on the day of arrival (or at a state park ranger station) before taking a site, and no self-pay envelopes are taken on site. The group camp ($50) is reserved through ReserveMN up to 120 days ahead.

Same-day advance payments are available for individual and equestrian campsites.'; 'Reservations for group campsites can be made up to 120 days in advance') + https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-forests/fees-reservations.html ('Group campsites $50'; Willow River Campground listed among campgrounds with group campsites; 'DNR does not accept self-payment envelopes on site or mail-in payments.'), read 2026-11-11

values.note: Minnesota state forest individual campsite, taxes included ($22 applies only to equestrian sites, none here). Paid online on the arrival date or at a state park ranger station. DNR state forest fee page, read 2026-11-11.

fees.source: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-forests/fees-reservations.html ('$17 - $22'; 'Starting in 2026 ... $17 per night ($22 for equestrian)'; 'Fees include taxes.') + DNR record cmp00018 (fee 1; no equestrian sites), read 2026-11-11

note: Primitive General C.C. Andrews State Forest campground just west of I-35 at Willow River, run from Banning State Park: spacious wooded back-in sites in two loops on a peninsula in Stanton Lake (the Willow River Flowage), with a paved boat ramp. --Claude
summary: DNR record, facility map and fee page read: 36 drive-in + 2 accessible primitive sites and a group camp, hand-pump water, vault toilets, individual sites first come ($17 paid online same day; the old 'reservable' was the group camp only). Not a horse camp, not an OHV base. Note's 'Zalesky Lake' corrected to Stanton Lake. Not waterfront kept with a lakeview lead; phone and link corrected.
flags: HORSE CAMP check (as asked): not a horse camp. The DNR record lists no equestrian sites (no $22 equestrian fee applies), no horse trail miles (horseback_miles 0) and no horse facilities; the DNR describes a primitive drive-in campground with a group camp. OHV: the forest has 37 mi of OHM/ATV trails, but the DNR trail page puts their parking at the McCormick Lake and Dago Lake day-use areas, not the campground, so this is not an OHV staging campground.

WATERFRONT not waterfront kept; lakeview LEAD for the reviewer (DNR claim contrary to the stored value). The DNR record says 'Several of the sites are along Stanton Lake.' The 2017 DNR map labels the water 'Former Stanton Lake (Willow River Flowage)', but current Esri imagery shows the flowage full of water on both the west and south sides of the campground peninsula. The western loop's site clearings (map sites 18-30; clearings around 46.3266,-92.8314, 46.3262,-92.8315 and 46.3260,-92.8313) sit roughly 20-40 m from the water, every one behind a band of trees; the east loop (sites 1-17, 31-38) is 100 m+ back. No site is on open ground within ~50 m, so no waterfront value; a filtered view from the west-end sites is plausible but no site photo confirms it, so it stays not waterfront unless the reviewer accepts a lakeview.

NOTE: the old note's 'along Zalesky Lake' is wrong: the DNR record and map name the water Stanton Lake / the Willow River Flowage. The old 'reservable online/by phone' described the group camp only; individual sites are first come with same-day online payment.
Season: the DNR record states no campground season; left unknown.

PIN 46.3283,-92.8262 sits in the east loop; the DNR facility point 46.327617,-92.828055 is near the middle of the two loops, about 160 m west-southwest. Under 250 m; the DNR point would be a better centroid if wanted.
